roots.name: Reasoning
roots.scope: Methods for transforming intellectual material, with their input, intended contribution, operating conditions, or construction at issue.

roots.name: Question
roots.scope: The distinction requested by a question, its possible resolutions, or its relation to a response.

roots.name: Claim
roots.scope: The content, support, or recorded acceptance of an assertion. Target facts retain their substantive subject.

roots.name: Expression
roots.scope: The form used to express identified content, or its interpretation by a specified recipient.

roots.name: Goal
roots.scope: Intended outcomes or their achievement conditions.

roots.name: Commitment
roots.scope: An agent undertaking an option or treating it as an operative instruction.

roots.name: Preference
roots.scope: What a specified agent favors in specified circumstances, or an account of that favoring.

roots.name: Criterion
roots.scope: An explicit standard governing a specified comparison or decision.

roots.name: Comparison
roots.scope: Comparison structures studied across target kinds, with the standard held fixed. Target-specific comparisons retain their qualified subjects.

roots.name: Explanation
roots.scope: The relation between an explanatory account and the occurrence or contrast it purports to explain.

roots.name: Prediction
roots.scope: A forecast specified before its outcome is available to the predictor.

roots.name: Problem
roots.scope: A specified obstruction relative to a requirement, or a remedy's adequacy to that obstruction.

roots.name: Plan
roots.scope: Prospective ordering of activities, prerequisites, or conditional continuations. Question-specific routes have their qualified Question entries.

roots.name: Resource
roots.scope: Means available for a specified use, including their capacities or feasible configurations.

roots.name: Memory
roots.scope: Continuity with earlier material under the identity and context needed for later use.

roots.name: Discovery
roots.scope: An increase in what is available to a specified inquirer relative to an explicit earlier position.

roots.name: Attention
roots.scope: Which available material receives operative focus under specified conditions.

roots.name: Execution
roots.scope: Actual control states of an adopted activity, with its substantive result kept distinct.

roots.name: Capability
roots.scope: Usable ability under specified conditions; includes the qualified Intelligence and Understanding refinements below.

roots.name: Intelligence
roots.scope: Adaptive use of available abilities when the appropriate means are not fixed in advance; a capability refinement, not an exclusive peer of all Capability.

roots.name: Understanding
roots.scope: Usable grasp of specified relations; a capability refinement that can overlap Intelligence rather than an exclusive alternative to it.

roots.name: Learning
roots.scope: Experience-dependent change in subsequent capability or conduct.

roots.name: Inquiry
roots.scope: Investigative organization studied as a method for establishing or revising findings.

roots.name: Relation
roots.scope: Predicates or their composition studied across target kinds; local instances remain qualified by their own subjects.

roots.name: Design
roots.scope: Relations among requirements, candidate forms, feasibility, or use studied across artifact kinds. Particular artifacts retain their own construction subjects.

roots.name: System
roots.scope: Specified systems as designed artifacts, including custom descendants, interfaces, or observed executions.

roots.name: Improvement
roots.scope: Comparative betterment of a changed item against a baseline under a specified standard. The change process is a separate subject.

roots.name: Subject
roots.scope: Specified matters of consideration, their names, boundaries, or relationships.

roots.name: Perception
roots.scope: Detection, discrimination, or identification from specified sensory presentations.

roots.name: Action
roots.scope: Specified behavioral responses and conditions governing their selection or inhibition.

roots.name: Reward
roots.scope: Expected rewarding outcomes, assigned value, and discrepancies from their occurrence.

roots.name: Shape
roots.scope: Form and orientation of represented shapes, including defined human representational tasks.

roots.name: Model
roots.scope: Specified token, attention, position, or parameter computations in computational models.

roots.name: Measurement
roots.scope: Defined quantities, instruments, observable proxies, and measurement result properties.

roots.name: Integer
roots.scope: Specified properties and decompositions of integers.

roots.name: Graph
roots.scope: Defined connectivity, path costs, and equivalence of graph structures.

roots.name: Equation
roots.scope: Existence or uniqueness of admissible solutions to specified equation systems.

roots.name: Price
roots.scope: Demand response to specified price variation.

roots.name: Exchange
roots.scope: Feasibility or incentive properties of specified exchange allocations.

roots.name: Production
roots.scope: Input requirements and costs of specified output production.

roots.name: Business
roots.scope: Customer demand and cash requirements within specified commercial activity.

roots.name: Rule
roots.scope: Authority, scope, interpretation, compliance, revision, or effects of specified rules.

roots.name: Norm
roots.scope: Justificatory grounds for specified normative conclusions.

roots.name: Object
roots.scope: Criteria for an object's identity over specified changes.

roots.name: Experience
roots.scope: Discriminable qualitative aspects of specified experiences.

roots.name: Narrative
roots.scope: Presentation of represented events and defined responses of specified audiences.

roots.name: Perspective
roots.scope: Configurations through which specified differences become consequential for an entity or interaction, including interpretive organizations and their formation, use, comparison or revision. Consciousness and deliberate selection are not required; bearer and mechanism are case-specific matters.

roots.name: Anticipation
roots.scope: Represented or inferred expectations of possible later events and their role in preparing, selecting or constructing subsequent activity.

roots.name: Uncertainty
roots.scope: Unresolved alternatives relative to a specified agent, information state and target, including how their resolution affects work.

roots.name: Conflict
roots.scope: Specified conditions that cannot jointly be met, and the means or effects of resolving that incompatibility.

roots.name: Deviation
roots.scope: A specified departure from a reference, with its extent, causes, consequences and attainable quality kept distinct.

roots.name: Game
roots.scope: Specified participant payoffs and their invariance over an admitted outcome domain.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach selection
subjects.settles: Choose an identifiable reasoning approach from a nonempty candidate set available at the time of choice for a specified matter; the selection rule may be implicit or explicit.
subjects.excludes: Creating an approach as part of a larger workflow, proving the choice optimal, or executing it.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach creation
subjects.settles: Construct a reasoning approach absent from the stated initial inventory, with executable intellectual operations.
subjects.excludes: Retrieving an existing approach under a new name.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach modification
subjects.settles: Produce a changed version of an identified reasoning approach with the changed operations explicit.
subjects.excludes: Claiming the revision is better without a comparison.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach identification
subjects.settles: Identify which approach a description or performance instantiates under stated identity conditions.
subjects.excludes: Choosing whether to use it.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach applicability
subjects.settles: Determine whether an approach's operating assumptions hold for the specified case.
subjects.excludes: Ranking several applicable approaches.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach comparison
subjects.settles: Determine the differences between candidate approaches under fixed comparison criteria.
subjects.excludes: Adopting the preferred candidate.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach selection criterion
subjects.settles: Specify what should govern choosing among reasoning approaches for the stated class of matters.
subjects.excludes: Making a particular choice under an already fixed criterion.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach requirement
subjects.settles: Specify what a proposed reasoning approach must accomplish under stated conditions.
subjects.excludes: Prescribing its internal steps.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach input specification
subjects.settles: Specify the intellectual material an approach accepts, including required distinctions.
subjects.excludes: Establishing that the supplied premises are true.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach output specification
subjects.settles: Specify the contribution whose production counts as executing the approach.
subjects.excludes: Proving the contribution is correct.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach assumption identification
subjects.settles: Identify the assumptions on which the approach's operations rely.
subjects.excludes: Establishing whether those assumptions hold in a particular case.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach composition
subjects.settles: Construct an arrangement of approaches with explicit intermediate contributions.
subjects.excludes: Merely listing compatible approach names.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach substitution
subjects.settles: Determine whether one approach can replace another while preserving the specified required contribution.
subjects.excludes: General similarity of their descriptions.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach termination condition
subjects.settles: Specify when further execution of the approach should stop for the stated purpose.
subjects.excludes: Reporting that a particular execution stopped.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach failure diagnosis
subjects.settles: Locate the approach feature responsible for a specified failure under an explicit failure account.
subjects.excludes: Treating every unsuccessful result as evidence of an approach defect.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach transfer condition
subjects.settles: Determine which changes of target preserve the applicability of the approach's transformation.
subjects.excludes: Inferring transfer from reuse of the same vocabulary.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning candidate space specification
subjects.settles: Specify which possibilities the reasoning process can currently consider.
subjects.excludes: Enumerating only the candidates already generated.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning candidate generation
subjects.settles: Produce possibilities within a specified reasoning candidate space.
subjects.excludes: Claiming that the space includes every relevant possibility.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning candidate exclusion
subjects.settles: Establish why an identified possibility can be removed under a stated exclusion condition.
subjects.excludes: Removing a possibility merely because it is inconvenient.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning candidate space expansion
subjects.settles: Add a distinct candidate dimension or admissible region absent from the earlier space.
subjects.excludes: Producing more candidates within the unchanged space.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning assumption consequence derivation
subjects.settles: Derive what follows if an identified assumption is accepted under stated inference rules.
subjects.excludes: Establishing that the assumption actually holds.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning assumption alternative construction
subjects.settles: Construct a specified alternative to an assumption that changes a consequential implication.
subjects.excludes: A caution compatible with the original assumption.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning error location
subjects.settles: Identify the particular intellectual step that fails a stated correctness condition.
subjects.excludes: Locating the implementation defect that caused the step to be made.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning error correction
subjects.settles: Replace the identified faulty intellectual step with a defensible contribution.
subjects.excludes: Merely recording that an error was noticed.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach specification
subjects.settles: Specify the operations and their composition that constitute an identified approach.
subjects.excludes: Claiming a newly written specification describes a newly invented approach.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach execution
subjects.settles: Perform the specified intellectual transformations on the supplied material.
subjects.excludes: Merely naming or describing the selected approach.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach retrieval
subjects.settles: Locate an existing approach matching an identified intellectual transformation need.
subjects.excludes: Selecting it as best among available candidates.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach representation
subjects.settles: Express an identified approach so its prescribed transformations can be recovered.
subjects.excludes: Constructing different transformations while claiming only a clearer description.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach execution fidelity
subjects.settles: Determine whether a particular performance followed the specified approach.
subjects.excludes: Establishing that faithful execution helped the task.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach contribution adequacy
subjects.settles: Determine whether the approach's actual output supplies the fixed required intellectual contribution.
subjects.excludes: Inferring usefulness solely from procedure compliance.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach cost estimation
subjects.settles: Estimate the stated time or resource demand of using an approach in the specified case.
subjects.excludes: Ranking approaches without fixing their required contribution.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning approach retirement
subjects.settles: Remove an identified approach from the operative candidate inventory under stated reasons.
subjects.excludes: Deleting its historical source identity.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning contribution requirement
subjects.settles: Specify which kind of intellectual contribution would change the current unresolved matter.
subjects.excludes: Prescribing one existing procedure before identifying the contribution needed.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Reasoning contribution selection
subjects.settles: Choose the next kind of contribution from the specified available alternatives.
subjects.excludes: Choosing among approaches that produce an already fixed contribution kind.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question specification
subjects.settles: Specify what a question asks about, including its requested distinction.
subjects.excludes: Choosing whether asking it is worthwhile.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question identity
subjects.settles: Determine whether two formulations request the same distinction under fixed interpretation.
subjects.excludes: Matching their wording.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question presupposition
subjects.settles: Identify what must be taken for granted for the question's requested distinction to apply.
subjects.excludes: Accepting that presupposition as true.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question scope
subjects.settles: Determine the referents, cases, or time range covered by what is asked.
subjects.excludes: Selecting the audience for the wording.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question candidate creation
subjects.settles: Construct a question specification introducing a stated unresolved distinction.
subjects.excludes: Producing another wording of an already identical question.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question candidate modification
subjects.settles: Revise an identified question's requested distinction or conditions.
subjects.excludes: Changing only its typography.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question candidate selection
subjects.settles: Choose which already specified question to pursue under fixed criteria.
subjects.excludes: Constructing an answer-dependent route through several questions.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question answer space specification
subjects.settles: Specify what differences among possible answers the question permits.
subjects.excludes: Treating the currently listed answers as exhaustive without grounds.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question answer fit
subjects.settles: Determine whether a response addresses the question's requested distinction with its interpretation fixed.
subjects.excludes: Determining whether the response is true.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question answer completeness
subjects.settles: Identify which parts of the requested resolution a response supplies or leaves unsettled.
subjects.excludes: Asking whether the answer is exhaustive outside the question's scope.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question answer presupposition correction
subjects.settles: Determine how rejecting a false presupposition resolves the original request.
subjects.excludes: Silently answering an unrelated question.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question answer equivalence
subjects.settles: Determine whether two responses settle the same requested distinctions.
subjects.excludes: Requiring identical sentences.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question route specification
subjects.settles: Specify which next question follows from each relevant answer condition.
subjects.excludes: Changing the identity of an individual question.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question route branch distinction
subjects.settles: Determine which answer differences require different continuations.
subjects.excludes: Branching on wording that changes no next investigation.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question route gap detection
subjects.settles: Find an admissible answer for which the stated route lacks an appropriate continuation.
subjects.excludes: A missing answer to an unrelated question.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question route termination condition
subjects.settles: Specify which resolved distinctions make further traversal unnecessary for the stated purpose.
subjects.excludes: Exhausting an arbitrary number of turns.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question answer construction
subjects.settles: Construct a response that supplies the requested distinction with any unresolved truth claims explicit.
subjects.excludes: Assuming structural responsiveness establishes correctness.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question answer revision
subjects.settles: Change a specified response to repair an identified failure to address the fixed question.
subjects.excludes: Revising a claim solely because it is false when answer fit was already satisfied.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Question route continuation selection
subjects.settles: Choose the applicable continuation after a specified answer is available.
subjects.excludes: Designing the route's branch rules.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim content specification
subjects.settles: Specify what an assertion says under an explicit interpretation.
subjects.excludes: Establishing whether its assertion is true.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim content reference
subjects.settles: Identify what the assertion's expressions refer to in the stated context.
subjects.excludes: Checking whether evidence supports the assertion.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim content quantifier scope
subjects.settles: Determine which cases an assertion ranges over and where its quantifiers apply.
subjects.excludes: Replacing an all-case claim with a typical-case claim.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim content qualification
subjects.settles: Specify the conditions restricting the assertion's applicability.
subjects.excludes: Quietly adding a condition after a counterexample.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim content equivalence
subjects.settles: Determine whether two assertions have the same stated content under a fixed interpretation.
subjects.excludes: Treating association or implication in one direction as identity.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim truth conditions
subjects.settles: Specify which situations make the identified proposition true under its interpretation.
subjects.excludes: Determining what the available evidence warrants.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim truth condition satisfaction
subjects.settles: Determine whether the specified situation satisfies a formalized proposition's truth conditions, with its domain facts supplied.
subjects.excludes: Absorbing collection of every substantive fact into a universal Truth subject.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim support identification
subjects.settles: Identify which reasons or observations bear on the specified claim and through what stated support relation.
subjects.excludes: Treating every cited source as support.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim support sufficiency
subjects.settles: Determine whether the supplied grounds meet a stated acceptance threshold for this claim.
subjects.excludes: Describing the agent's actual confidence.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim support limits
subjects.settles: Specify which conclusions remain unwarranted by the supplied grounds under the stated support rule.
subjects.excludes: Claiming that an unsupported conclusion is false.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim support dependence
subjects.settles: Determine which support paths rely on the same premise or source rather than providing independent grounds.
subjects.excludes: Counting repeated restatements as independent evidence.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim support defeater
subjects.settles: Identify a condition that undermines the specified support relation.
subjects.excludes: A generic warning compatible with that support remaining adequate.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim support preservation
subjects.settles: Determine which grounds still support the claim after a specified premise or source correction.
subjects.excludes: Discarding all support because one path failed.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim inference validity
subjects.settles: Determine whether the identified conclusion follows from the supplied premises under stated rules.
subjects.excludes: Establishing the truth of the premises.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim inference counterexample
subjects.settles: Construct an admissible case with true premises and a false conclusion for the specified inference.
subjects.excludes: A case with a false premise.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim acceptance status
subjects.settles: Determine whether an identified record treats the claim as accepted, rejected, conditional, or unresolved.
subjects.excludes: Establishing that this treatment is justified.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim acceptance confidence
subjects.settles: Identify the degree or form of confidence actually represented for the claim.
subjects.excludes: Inventing a probability where none is given.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim acceptance alternatives
subjects.settles: Specify which competing possibilities the record continues to leave open.
subjects.excludes: Treating an unmentioned possibility as ruled out.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim acceptance revision
subjects.settles: Determine which recorded claim status changes in response to a stated correction.
subjects.excludes: Claiming that the corrected record was subsequently used.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim inference specification
subjects.settles: Fix the premises, conclusion, and alleged consequence relation of the argument to be assessed.
subjects.excludes: Assessing an unspecified impression that the argument is convincing.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Claim inference revision
subjects.settles: Change the identified premises or inference step to address a demonstrated defect.
subjects.excludes: Claiming the unchanged conclusion must be false because its old argument failed.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression representation selection
subjects.settles: Choose a form for expressing fixed content under stated requirements.
subjects.excludes: Changing the content to make a chosen form convenient.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression representation creation
subjects.settles: Construct an expression that represents the specified content.
subjects.excludes: Establishing the truth of the content.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression representation modification
subjects.settles: Revise an existing expression with the intended content change or preservation explicit.
subjects.excludes: Assuming every edit preserves meaning.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression representation fidelity
subjects.settles: Determine which consequential content distinctions the representation preserves or loses.
subjects.excludes: Assuming readability proves fidelity.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression representation conversion
subjects.settles: Translate identified content into another representational form under an explicit correspondence.
subjects.excludes: Merely relabeling the existing form.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression representation ambiguity
subjects.settles: Identify distinct interpretations permitted by the representation under stated conventions.
subjects.excludes: Treating every unfamiliar expression as ambiguous.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression representation compression
subjects.settles: Reduce representational extent while specifying what information is retained or lost.
subjects.excludes: Claiming that shorter text necessarily contains the same distinctions.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression structure sequence
subjects.settles: Specify the order in which the expression presents identified contributions.
subjects.excludes: Changing the logical dependence among the contributions themselves.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression structure dependency visibility
subjects.settles: Determine whether the expression makes a specified dependency inspectable.
subjects.excludes: Establishing that the alleged dependency holds.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression structure grouping
subjects.settles: Determine which expressed contributions are grouped together under a stated representational distinction.
subjects.excludes: Inferring a subject taxonomy from page layout alone.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression wording selection
subjects.settles: Choose words for an identified content distinction under stated expression criteria.
subjects.excludes: Choosing what proposition to assert.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression wording modification
subjects.settles: Revise the verbal form of identified content with semantic differences recorded.
subjects.excludes: Calling an identity-to-correlation change a grammatical edit.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression interpretation attribution
subjects.settles: Determine what a specified recipient takes an expression to mean.
subjects.excludes: Inferring interpretation solely from a compliant-looking response.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression interpretation alignment
subjects.settles: Determine whether the attributed interpretation matches the specified intended content.
subjects.excludes: Establishing that the recipient acted on it.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression interpretation repair
subjects.settles: Produce a communicative change directed at a specified interpretation mismatch.
subjects.excludes: Repeating the original wording without addressing the mismatch.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression instruction requirement
subjects.settles: Specify what the expression directs its recipient to do under its intended interpretation.
subjects.excludes: Treating an implied unlimited permission as explicit instruction.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Expression instruction interpretation
subjects.settles: Determine what action requirement the recipient attributes to the instruction.
subjects.excludes: Establishing execution of that requirement.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Goal creation
subjects.settles: Construct a candidate intended outcome absent from the stated initial goal inventory.
subjects.excludes: Constructing a means to a fixed outcome.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Goal modification
subjects.settles: Revise the intended outcome or its scope while identifying what changed.
subjects.excludes: Changing only the route used to pursue it.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Goal identity
subjects.settles: Determine whether two formulations specify the same intended outcome.
subjects.excludes: Equating goals because they share a method.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Goal selection
subjects.settles: Choose an intended outcome from specified candidates under fixed criteria.
subjects.excludes: Committing to pursue the chosen outcome.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Goal achievement condition specification
subjects.settles: Specify what must be true for the goal to count as achieved.
subjects.excludes: Choosing a convenient indicator without establishing its relation to success.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Goal achievement indicator adequacy
subjects.settles: Determine how faithfully an indicator distinguishes goal achievement from non-achievement.

subjects.name: Capability evidence discrimination

subjects.name: Intelligence adaptation requirement

subjects.name: Intelligence adaptation strategy selection

subjects.name: Intelligence adaptation strategy construction
subjects.settles: Determine whether the agent can construct a fitting means when the stated available means are inadequate.

subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Intelligence adaptation transfer

subjects.name: Intelligence maintenance

subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Intelligence regression

subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Understanding content specification

subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Understanding content dependence

subjects.excludes: Treating every prerequisite document as a prerequisite understanding.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Understanding use application
subjects.settles: Determine whether the agent can use the identified relation to handle the specified case.

subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Understanding use explanation
subjects.settles: Determine whether the agent can reconstruct the identified relation for a stated explanatory task.

subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Understanding use transfer
subjects.settles: Determine whether the agent can use the relation in a changed representation or setting.
subjects.excludes: Recognizing identical surface wording.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Understanding error diagnosis
subjects.settles: Identify which relation the agent misconstrues or fails to use in the specified case.
subjects.excludes: Merely labeling the whole response unintelligent.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Learning change detection
subjects.settles: Determine which relevant ability or disposition changed after the specified experience.
subjects.excludes: Counting a changed stored note as sufficient behavioral evidence.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Learning change attribution
subjects.settles: Determine whether the identified change is attributable to the specified experience.
subjects.excludes: Inferring causation solely from before-after order.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Learning change retention
subjects.settles: Determine whether the experiential change persists across a specified interval.
subjects.excludes: Rechecking immediately under unchanged conditions alone.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Learning change transfer
subjects.settles: Determine whether the experiential change affects a specified new applicable case.
subjects.excludes: Assuming that a corrected example establishes transfer.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Learning change interference
subjects.settles: Identify how later experience alters an earlier learned ability under comparable conditions.

subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Learning correction uptake
subjects.settles: Determine whether a supplied correction changes the next applicable conduct.
subjects.excludes: Merely acknowledging or storing the correction.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Learning correction generalization
subjects.settles: Specify which further cases the correction legitimately governs.
subjects.excludes: Applying a local correction to every superficially related case.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Learning correction overgeneralization
subjects.settles: Identify a later use that extends the correction beyond its justified conditions.
subjects.excludes: Treating every broader application as an error.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Inquiry method selection
subjects.settles: Choose an investigative method for a specified subject and evidential purpose.

subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Inquiry method creation

subjects.excludes: Relabeling a generic workflow as a subject-specific science.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Inquiry method modification
subjects.settles: Revise a specified investigative organization in response to a concrete limitation.
subjects.excludes: Changing only the method's title.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Inquiry method assumption
subjects.settles: Identify the assumptions required by the method's route from observations to findings.
subjects.excludes: Establishing a particular factual claim's support.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Inquiry method limitation
subjects.settles: Identify a class of finding the specified investigative organization cannot establish under its conditions.
subjects.excludes: Claiming universal failure from one poorly executed use.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Inquiry test design
subjects.settles: Construct a test whose possible results distinguish the specified live alternatives.
subjects.excludes: Collecting observations that cannot separate those alternatives.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Inquiry test interpretation rule
subjects.settles: Specify how each possible test outcome changes the status of the alternatives.
subjects.excludes: Writing the interpretation only after observing the result.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Inquiry test confound
subjects.settles: Identify an alternative factor that prevents the planned observation from discriminating its target.
subjects.excludes: Listing unrelated possible problems.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Inquiry finding replication condition
subjects.settles: Specify what must be preserved for a repetition to test the same finding.
subjects.excludes: Requiring every irrelevant detail to be identical.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Inquiry finding revision condition
subjects.settles: Specify which result should revise the finding rather than only its stated application conditions.
subjects.excludes: Protecting every finding by adding exceptions indefinitely.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Relation predicate definition
subjects.settles: Specify what must hold between identified arguments for the stated relation predicate to apply.
subjects.excludes: Naming an association without its conditions.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Relation predicate direction
subjects.settles: Determine what changes when the argument order of the relation is reversed.
subjects.excludes: Assuming every relation is symmetric.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Relation predicate inverse
subjects.settles: Define the relation obtained by reversing a specified predicate's argument roles.
subjects.excludes: Treating inverse as logical negation.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Relation predicate negation
subjects.settles: Specify what denial of the stated relation rules out under its domain and quantifiers.
subjects.excludes: Treating not-a-subtype as disjointness.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Relation predicate necessity
subjects.settles: Determine whether the relation expresses a necessary condition for its stated consequent.
subjects.excludes: Inferring necessity from one successful route.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Relation predicate sufficiency
subjects.settles: Determine whether the relation establishes a sufficient condition under its stated scope.
subjects.excludes: Treating a helpful contribution as sufficient.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Relation composition validity

subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Relation composition domain
subjects.settles: Identify which argument domains make the proposed relation composition well formed.
subjects.excludes: Composing predicates whose intermediate arguments have different meanings.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Design requirement elicitation
subjects.settles: Derive a candidate requirement from identified contrasts among designs.
subjects.excludes: Retaining every feature of a favored example.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Design requirement justification
subjects.settles: Establish why the proposed requirement follows from the stated purpose or constraints.
subjects.excludes: Treating an observed preference as automatically mandatory.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Design requirement revision
subjects.settles: Change an identified requirement when a concrete alternative exposes a missing distinction.
subjects.excludes: Changing only how the requirement is worded.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Design requirement compatibility
subjects.settles: Determine whether the specified requirements admit at least one joint realization under fixed conditions.
subjects.excludes: Assuming separately satisfiable requirements are jointly satisfiable.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Design candidate space specification
subjects.settles: Specify the design dimensions and admissible values within the current design investigation.
subjects.excludes: Assuming the initial dimensions exhaust possible designs.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Design candidate contrast construction
subjects.settles: Construct alternatives that isolate a consequential design difference.
subjects.excludes: Comparing alternatives that differ on every feature without interpretation.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Design candidate feature attribution
subjects.settles: Determine which feature supports a specified contribution attributed to the design.
subjects.excludes: Assuming every feature caused the favorable judgment.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Design realization feasibility
subjects.settles: Determine whether the specified candidate can satisfy the stated cross-artifact realization constraints.
subjects.excludes: Resolving a target-specific implementation question by generic assertion.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Design realization requirement trace
subjects.settles: Identify where each specified requirement is realized or left unfulfilled in the candidate.
subjects.excludes: Counting a requirement's mention as its realization.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Design candidate construction
subjects.settles: Construct a design candidate that realizes specified selected aspects while making its other design choices explicit.
subjects.excludes: Assuming all features of a selected example are requirements.
subjects.source: Current naming derivation; source contribution exposes this missing target.

subjects.name: System identity specification
subjects.settles: Specify which artifact or version constitutes the named system.
subjects.excludes: Inferring a source identity from a similar project name.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: System identity lineage
subjects.settles: Establish the sources and deliberate departures that define a custom descendant.
subjects.excludes: Attributing the descendant's new operations to the original source.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: System purpose specification
subjects.settles: Specify the subject and result for which this particular system is being developed.
subjects.excludes: Treating relevance to a broad topic as a complete local design.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: System design creation
subjects.settles: Construct a purpose-specific system specification with actual objects, operations, and results.
subjects.excludes: Creating an empty directory or renamed source reference.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: System design modification
subjects.settles: Revise an identified system design with the changed behavior explicit.
subjects.excludes: Claiming the revision was implemented or effective without evidence.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: System design composition
subjects.settles: Construct a system arrangement whose intermediate results have explicit consumers.
subjects.excludes: Linking several project READMEs without a functioning design relation.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: System interface contract
subjects.settles: Specify the content, conditions, and failure meanings exchanged by identified system components.
subjects.excludes: Inferring compatibility from matching field names.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: System interface compatibility
subjects.settles: Determine whether a producer's specified output satisfies a consumer's specified input contract.
subjects.excludes: Declaring every interface question a collection of unrelated subjects.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: System interface failure propagation
subjects.settles: Determine which dependent results are affected by a specified interface failure.
subjects.excludes: Invalidating independent results without a dependency.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: System implementation correspondence
subjects.settles: Determine which behaviors of the specified design the implementation actually realizes.
subjects.excludes: Equating the written design with running behavior.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: System implementation execution evidence
subjects.settles: Identify which observed execution supports each specified implementation claim.
subjects.excludes: Treating a README demonstration as a verified run here.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Improvement comparison baseline
subjects.settles: Specify the earlier item or state against which improvement is claimed.
subjects.excludes: Selecting the baseline to hide an earlier better state.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Improvement comparison criterion
subjects.settles: Specify the fixed standard under which the changed item is judged better.
subjects.excludes: Inferring improvement from change alone.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Improvement comparison result
subjects.settles: Determine which stated respects are better, unchanged, or worse against the baseline.
subjects.excludes: Reporting only the favorable differences.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Improvement comparison criterion drift
subjects.settles: Determine whether an apparent improvement depends on changing the evaluative standard.
subjects.excludes: Treating a changed criterion as an improved artifact.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Improvement effect persistence
subjects.settles: Determine how long the demonstrated betterment survives under specified conditions.
subjects.excludes: Assuming an immediate gain persists indefinitely.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Improvement effect transfer
subjects.settles: Determine whether the betterment also holds in a specified changed context under a comparable standard.
subjects.excludes: Generalizing from one favorable example.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Improvement effect attribution
subjects.settles: Determine what explains the identified comparative betterment.
subjects.excludes: Assuming the latest intervention caused it.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject scope specification
subjects.settles: Specify what determination belongs to the subject with consequential context explicit.
subjects.excludes: Naming a topic without stating what is to be considered.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject scope identity
subjects.settles: Determine whether two descriptions specify the same matter under a fixed interpretation.
subjects.excludes: Treating different names as proof of distinct subjects.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject scope inclusion
subjects.settles: Establish that every matter admitted by a proposed child definition is admitted by its parent.
subjects.excludes: Inferring inclusion from useful contribution or word order.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject scope overlap
subjects.settles: Construct a single specified matter admitted by both proposed alternative definitions.
subjects.excludes: A document that merely contains two different matters.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject scope exclusion
subjects.settles: Establish why no specified matter can satisfy both fixed alternative definitions.
subjects.excludes: Treating a failed inclusion test as disjointness.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject scope gap
subjects.settles: Identify a specified matter covered by none of the candidate scopes within the declared coverage domain.
subjects.excludes: Claiming universal completeness because every current row has a home.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject name construction
subjects.settles: Construct a literal general-first name for a specified subject without joining distinct targets.
subjects.excludes: Generating a label before identifying its matter.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject name ambiguity
subjects.settles: Identify materially different readings permitted by the proposed subject name.
subjects.excludes: Assuming a fluent phrase has one exact meaning.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject name equivalence
subjects.settles: Determine whether two names are aliases for the same defined subject.
subjects.excludes: Counting aliases as newly discovered subjects.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject name revision
subjects.settles: Replace a subject name while recording whether the underlying scope changed.
subjects.excludes: Concealing a new definition as a cosmetic rename.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject hierarchy construction
subjects.settles: Construct containment relations among already defined subjects within a stated coverage domain.
subjects.excludes: Imposing a tree whose sibling scopes still overlap.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject hierarchy collision repair
subjects.settles: Revise or merge definitions after a single specified matter fits two proposed siblings.
subjects.excludes: Choosing a preferred home while retaining the collision.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Subject hierarchy coverage
subjects.settles: Determine whether every matter in a specified finite test domain is admitted by the hierarchy.
subjects.excludes: Inferring coverage of all possible subjects from the finite test.
subjects.source: Current user naming direction; derivation from the recorded scope definitions.

subjects.name: Criterion application result
subjects.settles: Determine the result of applying a specified criterion to identified material under fixed application conditions.
subjects.excludes: Justifying the criterion or checking consistency across several applications.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Current user direction and attached expansion note

subjects.name: Explanation account adequacy
subjects.settles: Determine whether a proposed account resolves its specified explanatory contrast under stated adequacy conditions.
subjects.excludes: Selecting among accounts or claiming that an adequate explanation is uniquely possible.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Current user direction and attached expansion note

subjects.name: Reasoning approach availability
subjects.settles: Determine which reasoning approaches a specified agent can access in a usable representation at the time of choice.
subjects.excludes: Existence somewhere, applicability to this case, recognition by the agent, or authorization to execute.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Current user direction and attached expansion note

subjects.name: Reasoning approach repertoire coverage
subjects.settles: Determine which specified reasoning needs have at least one represented approach in an identified repertoire.
subjects.excludes: Choosing an approach for one case or proving universal completeness of reasoning.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Current user direction and attached expansion note

subjects.name: Relation pattern extraction
subjects.settles: Identify a stated relational structure shared by specified cases while omitting designated incidental features.
subjects.excludes: Mapping that structure to a further case or claiming that every abstraction is relational.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Current user direction and attached expansion note

subjects.name: Relation pattern case mapping
subjects.settles: Determine which elements of a target case can occupy the roles of a specified relational pattern.
subjects.excludes: Creating the pattern or establishing that mapped objects share every property.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Current user direction and attached expansion note

subjects.name: Memory record availability
subjects.settles: Determine which identified records are accessible to an agent through specified routes at a stated time.
subjects.excludes: A record existing elsewhere or being successfully retrieved in a particular attempt.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Current user direction and attached expansion note

subjects.name: Memory record source attribution
subjects.settles: Determine which origin produced a remembered or stored item, including perceived, imagined, inferred, or externally supplied origins.
subjects.excludes: Determining whether its content is true; an accurately attributed report can be false.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Current user direction and attached expansion note

subjects.name: Memory record retrieval interference
subjects.settles: Determine how competing records change retrieval of a specified target under fixed cues.
subjects.excludes: Total storage capacity or loss of the target record itself.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Current user direction and attached expansion note

subjects.name: Memory active content maintenance
subjects.settles: Determine how identified content remains usable over a specified delay within an active task.
subjects.excludes: Long-term record retention or replacing the active content.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; NIMH RDoC domain and construct definitions

subjects.name: Memory active content update
subjects.settles: Determine how active task content is replaced or revised following a specified input.
subjects.excludes: Maintaining unchanged content or proving the revision correct.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; NIMH RDoC domain and construct definitions

subjects.name: Memory active content capacity
subjects.settles: Determine how much specified content can remain usable under stated active-task conditions.
subjects.excludes: Capacity in all possible tasks or total stored knowledge.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; NIMH RDoC domain and construct definitions

subjects.name: Goal representation maintenance
subjects.settles: Determine how a represented intended outcome remains available to govern activity over a stated interval.
subjects.excludes: Choosing the outcome or establishing its achievement.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; NIMH RDoC domain and construct definitions

subjects.name: Perception signal discrimination
subjects.settles: Determine whether specified sensory inputs can be distinguished by an agent under stated conditions.
subjects.excludes: Correctly identifying the external cause of each input.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; NIMH RDoC domain and construct definitions

subjects.name: Perception signal detection
subjects.settles: Determine whether an agent detects a specified signal against a stated background.
subjects.excludes: Distinguishing two detected signals or identifying their cause.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; NIMH RDoC domain and construct definitions

subjects.name: Perception object identification
subjects.settles: Determine which candidate object a specified sensory presentation represents.
subjects.excludes: Establishing the object's persistence across time or its real existence from presentation alone.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; NIMH RDoC domain and construct definitions

subjects.name: Action response selection
subjects.settles: Determine which candidate behavioral response is selected under specified task conditions.
subjects.excludes: General reasoning approach choice or whether the chosen response is executed.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; NIMH RDoC domain and construct definitions

subjects.name: Action response inhibition
subjects.settles: Determine whether a specified response is withheld or stopped following a stated condition.
subjects.excludes: Selecting another response or permanently removing the capacity to respond.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; NIMH RDoC domain and construct definitions

subjects.name: Reward outcome anticipation
subjects.settles: Determine what rewarding outcome an agent expects before the relevant event.
subjects.excludes: The outcome actually received or the pleasure it produces.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; NIMH RDoC domain and construct definitions

subjects.name: Reward outcome valuation
subjects.settles: Determine the value an agent assigns to a specified rewarding outcome under stated conditions.
subjects.excludes: Its objective benefit under an external goal or its delivery probability alone.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; NIMH RDoC domain and construct definitions

subjects.name: Reward prediction error
subjects.settles: Determine the discrepancy between an expected rewarding outcome and its observed occurrence under a fixed coding rule.
subjects.excludes: The rule by which that discrepancy changes later behavior.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; NIMH RDoC domain and construct definitions

subjects.name: Shape orientation specification
subjects.settles: Specify a shape's orientation relative to an identified reference frame.
subjects.excludes: The shape's intrinsic form or position in space.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Shepard and Metzler, Mental Rotation of Three-Dimensional Objects (1971)

subjects.name: Shape representation rotation
subjects.settles: Determine the representation produced by changing a represented shape's orientation through a specified rotation in a stated frame.
subjects.excludes: Identifying the mechanism producing the transformation, timing it, or measuring its fidelity.
subjects.source: Meaning-aware revision from the current user note; prior scope preserved in Name Changes.

subjects.name: Shape orientation equivalence
subjects.settles: Determine whether two represented shapes coincide under an allowed rotation and translation.
subjects.excludes: Equivalence permitting reflection or scaling unless separately allowed.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Shepard and Metzler, Mental Rotation of Three-Dimensional Objects (1971)

subjects.name: Shape mirror equivalence
subjects.settles: Determine whether one represented shape coincides with a reflected version of another under specified alignment rules.
subjects.excludes: Equivalence by rotation alone.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Current user direction and attached expansion note

subjects.name: Shape representation rotation mechanism
subjects.settles: Identify the operations or physical processes producing a specified rotation of a shape representation in an identified implementation.

subjects.source: Meaning-aware revision from the current user note; prior scope preserved in Name Changes.

subjects.name: Shape representation rotation duration
subjects.settles: Determine how long a specified representational rotation takes under defined task conditions.
subjects.excludes: Time attributable only to orientation change when measured response time also contains other stages.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Shepard and Metzler, Mental Rotation of Three-Dimensional Objects (1971)

subjects.name: Shape representation rotation accuracy
subjects.settles: Determine how faithfully a specified representational rotation preserves the required shape relations.
subjects.excludes: Response speed or accuracy of unrelated spatial abilities.
subjects.source: Authored subject definition; Shepard and Metzler, Mental Rotation of Three-Dimensional Objects (1971)

subjects.name: Model token sequence representation
subjects.settles: Specify how a model's input symbols are represented as an ordered token sequence under a fixed vocabulary.
